issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect Course.instructor to be a String (a single string, e.g. "Matthias, Patrick, and Felix"), but the solution repository defines Course.instructor as [String] (an array of strings). This is a structural type mismatch: the solution's Course initializer signature uses instructor: [String] while the Client in the solution still constructs the Course by passing a String. This inconsistency will confuse students and can cause the solution code to be non-compilable or to behave unexpectedly (e.g. printing an array instead of an instructor name) and prevents a straightforward mapping from the problem description and template to the provided solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Course.instructor type consistent across artifacts. The simplest fix (and consistent with the problem statement and template) is to change the solution repository to use instructor: String: update solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift so instructor is declared as String and the initializer parameter is instructor: String (assigning self.instructor = instructor). Ensure any code that prints the instructor (e.g. Developer.attend) treats it as a String. Alternatively, if you intend instructor to be an array of names, update the problem statement and template to require [String] and ensure Client constructs and prints an array accordingly. Prefer keeping instructor as String to match the exercise description and the template.
